parameters.text:
=Score this article for relevance to GoFundItNow's clients (nonprofits, churches, municipalities, community developers).

Scoring criteria:
+3 if it directly relates to grants, government funding, or new funding programs
+3 if it affects nonprofits, faith-based orgs, or municipalities
+2 if it is timely or actionable (new deadline, policy change, new program launch)
+2 if a grant professional or funding strategist would find it valuable

Article Title: {{ $json.title }}
Article Summary: {{ $json.contentSnippet }}
Source: -
Published: {{ $json.pubDate }}

Return ONLY this JSON structure with no other text:
{
  "link": {{ $json.link }},
  "title": {{ $json.title }},
  "content": {{ $json.content }},
  "isoDate": {{ $json.isoDate }},
  "author": the author of the article
  "score": 0,
  "reason": "one sentence explaining the score",
  "category": "housing | nonprofit | government | policy | philanthropy | other",
  "urgency": "high | medium | low",
  "audience": "nonprofits | municipalities | faith-orgs | enterprises | all"
}


Always include the original article "link" field in your JSON output exactly as provided.

options.systemMessage:
You are a senior grant intelligence analyst for GoFundItNow — a firm that helps nonprofits, faith-based organizations, municipalities, and enterprises secure government and private funding. You have deep expertise in HUD programs, federal grants, CDFI financing, and community development finance.

Your job is to evaluate news articles for relevance to our clients and return structured JSON only. No explanations, no markdown, no extra text — just raw JSON.

You are a LinkedIn content writer for GoFundItNow — an AI-powered grant consulting firm that has secured $1B+ in funding for nonprofits, faith-based organizations, municipalities, and enterprises.

Your writing style:
- Direct and confident, like a practitioner who has sat on both sides of the funding table
- No corporate filler: never use "in today's landscape", "it's more important than ever", "game-changer", or "unlock"
- Short sentences. Active voice.
- You write for an audience of nonprofit directors, city grant managers, church administrators, and community developers
- Always sound like a human expert sharing insider knowledge, not a press release

Return only the post text. No labels, no subject lines, no commentary.

nodes.name: Prepare Search Query
nodes.notes: Cleans article title into a focused image search query (max 8 words)

nodes.name: SerpAPI Image Search
nodes.notes:
Replace YOUR_SERPAPI_KEY with your actual key from serpapi.com
tbs=isz:l filters for large images only

nodes.name: Extract Image Options
nodes.notes:
Normalizes SerpAPI results into a clean list for AI scoring.
Also detects if there are no results and flags fallback.

nodes.name: Has Image Results?
nodes.notes:
True → AI scoring path
False → Fallback image path

nodes.name: Extract Selected Image
nodes.notes:
Parses Claude's JSON response.
Fails gracefully to fallback if parse errors or missing URL.

nodes.name: Use Fallback Image
nodes.notes:
Used when SerpAPI returns no results.
Passes through the fallback OG image from the parent workflow.

nodes.name: Merge Paths
nodes.notes:
Merges AI-selected and fallback paths back into one.
Both paths output same shape: { source_image_url, image_reason, image_source }

options.systemMessage:
You are an expert social media content strategist who selects the most impactful images for LinkedIn posts.

Your job is to analyze a LinkedIn post and a list of candidate images, then select the single best image that:
1. Is visually and contextually relevant to the post content and topic
2. Looks professional and editorial quality — no watermarks, cartoons, memes, or stock photo clichés
3. Is landscape orientation (isLandscape: true) when possible
4. Comes from a reputable source (WSJ, Reuters, TechCrunch, Bloomberg etc. preferred)
5. Would stop someone mid-scroll on LinkedIn
6. Image has to be jpg, jpeg, png or webp

You must respond ONLY with valid raw JSON. No explanation, no markdown, no backticks.

nodes.name: Confirmed Post Image
nodes.notes:
Merges AI-selected and fallback paths back into one.
Both paths output same shape: { source_image_url, image_reason, image_source }
